_readme: Shared PHP<->JS lockstep fixture for #2073 commit 8 (voice/echo render). Loaded by tests/test-voice-render-lockstep.js, which runs the REAL includes/voice_parts_render.php (via a single batched `php -r` call, the tests/test-org-logo-resolver-lockstep.js pattern) and the REAL js/modules/voice-parts-render.js against the exact same inputs and asserts (a) the two agree with each other and (b) both agree with this file's own hand-derived `expect` value, from Design-pass-5 (.claude/vocal-parts-2073-plan.md) SS1.2/SS1.4's worked examples. KNOWN, DOCUMENTED QUIRK: PHP's htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES) escapes an apostrophe as `'` while this project's own js/utils/html.js escapeHtml() escapes it as `'` -- both are valid, equally-safe, IDENTICALLY-RENDERED numeric character references (no browser treats them differently), but they are not the same BYTES. The lockstep test normalises this one specific difference before comparing so it proves what actually matters here (span positions, class names, attribute values, code-point slicing) without going red over a pre-existing, harmless, unrelated inconsistency between two escaping utilities this commit did not introduce and is not in scope to fix.
